description.value: The study investigated the diagnostic value and clinical relevance of diffusion tensor imaging and FDG-PET for detecting cerebral alterations in early behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia.

spans.text: The aim of the current study was to investigate the diagnostic value of DTI in comparison to 18F-FDG-PET to detect cerebral alterations in a cohort of patients with early stages of bvFTD who were lacking frontal and temporal atrophy on conventional MRI.

description.value: Thirty patients with early stages of bvFTD and 42 healthy controls underwent neuroimaging and clinical assessment; patients were followed for at least 12 months.

spans.text: Images of the following MRI sequences were obtained: a native isotropic 3D magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo imaging (MPRAGE) T1- weighted sequence (voxel size 1.0 mm×1.0 mm×1.0 mm, slice thickness 1.0 mm, repetition time (TR) 1900 ms, 2.52 echo time (TE) ms, generalized autocalibrating partially parallel acquisition (GRAPPA) factor 2), an axial T2-weighted turbo spin- echo (TSE) (35 slices, voxel size 0.6 mm×0.4 mm×4.0 mm, slice thickness 4.0 mm, TR 4220 ms, TE 102 ms, slice order interlaced), and a fluid attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) (35 slices, voxel size 0.9 mm×0.9 mm×4.0 mm, TR 9000 ms, TE 93 ms, inversion time (TI) 2500 ms, slice order interlaced).
